title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, reconstructed from this and the neighbouring pages. L is a totally ordered set. M is the set of 'cells' of the associated 1-dimensional combinatorial space: points P_a (a in L) and open segments S_{a,b} (a<b). The symmetric relation X |o| Y means 'X and Y are disjoint' (étrangers). For X in M, the notation δX ≥ a means X lies in the closed half-line ≥ a, and δX ≤ x means X lies in the half-line ≤ x.

For a part Φ of M:
- cosupp°(Φ) = {Y : Y |o| X for all X in Φ}, a polar.
- Supp°(Φ) = cosupp°(cosupp°(Φ)), the bipolar or 'support'.

The page serves the computation of these supports, which the previous page states as Cor. 1–4. Examples: Supp(P_a) = {P_a}, and Supp(S_{a,b}) = the closed ombre (points P_x with a ≤ x ≤ b and segments inside [a,b]). The goal, announced on the next page ('4 juillet'), is to determine the 'polygones', i.e. the constructible sets in M.

Proof of Cor. 1 on this page. Let X be in Supp°(P_a).
- If a is the least or greatest element of L, every element of M other than P_a is disjoint from P_a. So cosupp°(P_a) = M − {P_a}. Irreflexivity of |o| (a nonempty cell is not disjoint from itself) then forces Supp°(P_a) = {P_a}.
- Otherwise choose x < a < y. Then S_{x,a} is in cosupp°(P_a), so X |o| S_{x,a}, so δX ≥ a or δX ≤ x.
- δX ≤ x is impossible. It would give X |o| P_a, i.e. X in cosupp°(P_a). But for any Φ, cosupp°(Φ) ∩ Supp°(Φ) = ∅, again by irreflexivity: an element of both would be disjoint from itself.
- Hence δX ≥ a. Symmetrically, using S_{a,y}, δX ≤ a, so X = P_a.

Cor. 2 (support of S_{a,b}) is handled the same way. One proves δX ≥ a, then δX ≤ b.
- If a is minimal, the first step is easy.
- Otherwise take x < a < b. Then S_{x,a} is in cosupp°(S_{a,b}), so δX ≤ x or δX ≥ a. The case δX ≤ x is excluded as before: it would make X disjoint from S_{a,b}, i.e. X in cosupp°(S_{a,b}).

The next page shows by counterexample (the poset a→b←c) that these statements fail when L is not totally ordered.
errors: No genuine mathematical error. Minor gap: Grothendieck writes 'X |o| a' for 'X |o| P_a'.
The use of δX (X lies in a half-line) is informal. The final step 'δX ≥ a and δX ≤ a imply X = P_a' needs only that δ encodes the closed hull of the cell, which is implicit.
In Cor. 2 only the first inequality is sketched, and the case where a is minimal is dismissed as easy. Fine for a total order.

ideas.what: Support of a set of cells defined as the bipolar (double orthogonal) for the symmetric irreflexive relation 'disjoint'; closure Supp = cosupp∘cosupp
ideas.modern_name: Galois connection / polarity of an orthogonality space; biorthogonal closure

ideas.what: Use of irreflexivity to get cosupp°(Φ) ∩ Supp°(Φ) = ∅
ideas.modern_name: standard property of polars in an orthogonality space

ideas.what: Combinatorial model of a 1-dimensional ordered stratified space (points and open segments) aimed at classifying 'polygones'/constructible sets, as part of a tame-topology programme
ideas.modern_name: cell decomposition / o-minimal-style tame topology in dimension 1; constructible sets on a finite poset space
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn (o-minimality, 1980s); Grothendieck's call for 'topologie modérée' in Esquisse (1984)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 announces tame topology, not this formalism

missed.claim: Grothendieck defines supports and shadows (ombres) of cells via the bipolar of the disjointness relation, i.e. he treats the cell complex as an orthogonality space. Topological closure-type operations are recovered as biorthogonal closures. This links his tame-topology project to orthogonality-space / polarity techniques from quantum logic and formal concept analysis, a link not made in the literature.
missed.quote: cos-supp°(𝔏) ∩ supp°(𝔏) = ∅, pour toute partie 𝔏 de M
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It suggests a purely relational (lattice-theoretic) axiomatization of constructible sets in tame/stratified spaces, but on this page it is only verified in the trivial 1-dimensional totally ordered case.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine verification of elementary lemmas, the supports of points and segments in a linearly ordered 1-dimensional cell model. The only mildly interesting feature is the polarity-based definition of support, part of the unpublished Analysis situs formalism, but the content of this page is elementary.
transcription_corrections: 'Alors $\not\in S_{x,a} \in \mathrm{cos-sp}^\circ(P_a)$' should read 'Alors $S_{x,a} \in \mathrm{cosupp}^\circ(P_a)$'. The stray symbol is the start of the word or a struck letter.
'anti-influence de |o|' (twice) is most likely 'antiréflexivité de |o|'. The argument uses exactly irreflexivity.
Last lines: roughly 'et la première [éventualité] est exclue comme ci-dessus, car on aurait X |o| S_{a,b}', i.e. X would lie in cosupp°(S_{a,b}).
'102' at bottom left is the archive folio number. '93' at top is Grothendieck's own pagination.
